_comment: Copy this file to live.config.json in this folder (git ignores that name), fill in a TEST account, start the game servers, then run: npm run test:live

Two limits of the servers can lock you out if you run this too often. (1) The certifier blocks the test account from an address for 15 seconds after one wrong password, and for 15 minutes after three in a row; a good login clears the count. A run sends one wrong password from this PC and one from the simulated address 10.0.0.1, so wait 15 seconds between runs. (2) Until the certifier and the login server are rebuilt with flood-limiter-gateway.patch and have a Gateway "127.0.0.1" line (server-patches/README.md), their accept limiter counts connections from one address that arrive less than 200 ms apart; after 50 of them it cuts every connection from that address for about 10 minutes, and the count never decays. The test keeps its connections 300 ms apart and ends each flow before the next, but do not loop it.

gateway: the test runs this gateway inside its own process. listen.port must be free (8091 does not clash with a gateway on 8090). trustedProxies must list 127.0.0.1, because the test simulates other addresses with X-Forwarded-For.

certifierPatched: set true only when the rebuilt Certifier.exe (server-patches/README.md) is running and Certifier.ini has a Gateway "127.0.0.1" line. It turns on the test that a wrong password from one address does not block another.

bannedTestAddress: an address you added to Program/IPCut.ini (restart the account server afterwards), for example "10.0.0.99", or null. It turns on the banned-address test, which also needs certifierPatched.
account, password, bankPin: a throwaway account with at least one empty character slot. The test creates WebTest and 3 digits in the first empty slot with this Bank PIN, then deletes it.

world: the world test (npm run test:live:world) is skipped without this section. accounts: two throwaway accounts with their Bank PINs; the first walks, the second watches. Each uses its first character, which must stand in Flaris within sight of the other's (a new character does); an account without a character gets WebWalk and 3 digits, made first and deleted at the end with its Bank PIN. It also needs gateway and certifierAddress above, and the servers running with the rebuilt WorldServer (world-snapshot-index.patch) and CacheServer (cache-client-addr.patch, with a Gateway "127.0.0.1" line in CacheServer.ini so the cache server takes the player's real address from the gateway). The converted game files must be in dist/assets (npm run convert). Leaving takes the world server a moment to save the character, so entering again straight after is turned away for a few seconds; the test waits up to 30 s for that. Run it once, not in a loop (the flood limit above counts its connections too).

The fight: the last part of the world test is a fight on the real servers (to run only that part: npm run test:live:world -- -t fight). The first account's character checks that its bag was read (it looks for the starter food: 3 lollipops and a biscuit), walks out of Flaris through the north gate and over the bridge to the field of Small Aibatts, picks the nearest one, and attacks it until it dies, for at most a minute. If the server says another player is already fighting that Aibatt, it picks another one, once. Then it checks that its EXP went up. The test fails if the server says the attack speed is wrong, if a swing gets no damage back within 3 seconds, if the EXP does not go up after the kill, or if any message from the server is misread. So the first account should have a new character, or a low-level one that still carries its starter food and stands where new characters start, beside Flaris's lodestar: a high-level character gets little or no EXP for a Small Aibatt. An account with no character is fine: the test makes a new one and deletes it at the end. A character the test did not make walks back to where it started afterwards. Small Aibatts must be alive on the field just outside Flaris's north gate (one that dies comes back within half a minute), and no other player should be fighting them. The converted game files in dist/assets must be up to date (npm run convert).
